Glossary & Appendices

The Governing Rules of High VysoanThe Full Glossary

Two things belong here rather than folded into earlier narrative: the governing rules of the High Vysoan tongue, and the full glossary of High Vysoan terms used throughout this article.

The Governing Rules of High Vysoan#

Every High Vysoan term used elsewhere in this article is gathered in the full glossary that follows this section; the tongue's own grammar, set down rule by rule rather than left buried in running prose, is kept here first, in a section of its own.

Pronunciation, Stress & Capitalization

RuleStatementExample
Marked-Vowel StressA marked long vowel (ā, ē, ī, ō, ū, ȳ) is always stressed, wherever it falls in the word.Kardārys — kahr-DAHR-ihs
Default StressA word carrying no marked vowel at all stresses its next-to-last syllable instead.Valzantys — vahl-ZAHN-tihs
CapitalizationA Vysoan word is capitalized only when it opens a sentence, or when it is itself a proper noun or title (a royal style, an epithet, a personal name) — an ordinary verb, noun, or adjective falling elsewhere in a sentence is written lower-case.Trēsyvēzos amīlōs, "Son of the Sun, lead us" — the title capitalized, the ordinary imperative that follows it not

The Definite & Indefinite Articles

RuleStatementExample
SingularThe suffix -ēr, placed directly after a noun, renders "the" for a singular.Kardārys → Kardārysēr, "the Kardārys"
Singular, Feminine (-yñ Nouns)Shifts to the allomorph -ār, matching -yñ's own vowel, rather than the tongue's usual -ēr.Kardāryñ → Kardāryñār, "the Empress"
PluralThe suffix -ēri renders "the" for a plural noun; the added -i follows the tongue's own Bare -r Ending rule for pluralization, set down among the Plural Formation rules below.Vēzgharzanti → Vēzgharzantiēri, "the Sunblood Sentinels"
Plural, Feminine (-yñ Nouns)Shifts to the allomorph -āri, for the same reason.Kardāryñi → Kardāryñiāri, "the Empresses"
ElisionA noun already ending in a bare -e loses that ending before the suffix is added, rather than carrying both.Vȳsōse → Vȳsōsēr, "the Vysoan"; Kardārōñe → Kardārōñēr, "the Imperial"
Placement in a Compound TitleThe suffix attaches to the phrase's head noun, never merely to its last word — a positional rule, not a semantic one.Dēmys Vȳsōse ("the Vysoan Throne") → Dēmysēr Vȳsōse, never Dēmys Vȳsōsēr
IndefiniteThe cardinal numeral Ēl ("one") stands before the noun as a free word, never suffixed, and serves also as the indefinite article.Ēl Kardārys, "a Kardārys"

Plural Formation

RuleStatementExample
Drop-and-Replace ClassA noun ending -ys, -os, or a bare -e drops that ending for a bare -i.Kardārys → Kardāri; Jehābaros → Jehābari; Kardārōñe → Kardārōñi
Additive ClassA noun ending -ion, -yr, -ar, -or, or -arz simply takes an added -i.Maegysombāzmion → Maegysombāzmioni; Sīvoktyr → Sīvoktyri; Maegysdār → Maegysdāri; Gaomagor → Gaomagori; Maegysdārarz → Maegysdārarzi
Additive Class, Feminine (-yñ Nouns)A noun ending -yñ follows this same Additive Class exactly: the ordinary added -i.Kardāryñ → Kardāryñi, "Empresses"
Bare -r EndingA noun — or a suffix, such as the definite article's own -ēr — already ending in a bare -r takes a simple added -i.Raqir → Raqiri, "Friends"; compare Vēzgharzantiēri, formed the same way from -ēr

The Genitive & Feminine Suffixes

RuleStatementExample
FormationThe suffix -e, pronounced "-eh," renders "of" when added to a noun.Kardārys → Kardāryse, "of the Kardārys"
Genitive PhrasesWhen a genitive phrase holds more than one word, the -e falls on its first word only, never repeated across the phrase; a single-word genitive takes the -e as before.Rȳarl Ōsare Āeksys, "Year of Our Lord" — the -e on Ōsar alone, not on Āeksys; contrast the single-word Dēmysēr Vȳsōse, "the Throne of Vysos"
Patronymic UseA father's own name takes the same -e suffix to form a Vysoan's patronymic, set between the given name and the family name.Āezāerys → Āezāeryse, in Āelyxanthor Āezāeryse Vēzgharyōñ
Feminine Formation (-yñ)Replaces a masculine noun's own ending outright, rather than being added atop it.Kardārys → Kardāryñ, "Empress"
Vowel MergerWhen the -e suffix is added to a word already ending in a bare -e — such as the possessive pronoun Ȳse, "His," standing alone — the two vowels do not double into "-ee"; they merge into one long, macroned -ē.Ȳse → Ȳsē, "of his"; as in Āezāerys, Ēlvesēr Ȳsē Rōz, "Āezāerys, the First of His Name"

The Tense Suffixes

RuleStatementExample
Past (-sīr)The suffix -sīr, added to a verb root, marks the past tense.Ūbre- → Ūbresīr, "Taught"
Future (-māz)The suffix -māz, added to a verb root, marks the future tense.Sa → Samāz, "Will be"
Continuous (sa + -en)The copula sa, followed by a verb's present participle in -en, forms the continuous aspect.Sa jemīlen, "Is protecting"

The -Kes Suffix

RuleStatementExample
Vowel-Final RootThe suffix -kes, meaning "in the likeness of" and functioning as the English -ly, attaches directly to a root already ending in a vowel.Vetti → Vettikes, "Lawfully"
Non-Vowel-Final RootIf the root instead ends in one or more non-vowels, all of them are dropped before -kes is suffixed to the vowel that remains.Vēdros → Vēdrokes, "Angrily"
Multiple Trailing Non-VowelsWhere more than one non-vowel stands at the root's end, all are dropped together, not merely the last.Hūrarl → Hūrakes, "Monthly"

The -Ēl Suffix

RuleStatementExample
Agent NounThe suffix -ēl, added to a verb root, forms a noun naming one who performs that action.Jemīl → Jemīlēl, "Protector"
Kinship with ĒlThe suffix is the noun Ēl, "One," set at the root's end: the agent is "the one who" does the deed. It is distinct from the participle in -en joined with ēli, which names a company by what it does, as Jemīlenēli, "Protecting Ones."Jaehēlēpēl, "the Breath Giver of God"
PluralAn agent noun in -ēl forms its plural in -ēli, as Ēl, "One," becomes Ēli, "Ones."Jemīlēl → Jemīlēli, "Protectors"

The Kar- Prefix

RuleStatementExample
Reservation to House VēzgharyōñThe prefix Kar-, already marking greatness in Kardārys and Karadēmys and set again before Drāzantys and its like, may be attached only to a personal name, a title of a person, or the name of a building or place belonging to, or descended from, House Vēzgharyōñ and its throne — never to any such name or title standing outside the house.Kardrāzantys, "Archduke," reserved to the Imperial House alone; contrast the plain Drāzantys, "Duke," a style any elevated house not of the blood may bear

Word Order & The Vocative Particle

RuleStatementExample
Flexible OrderWord order between a vocative address and the verb that follows is a matter of stylistic arrangement rather than fixed grammar; either the address or the verb may lead the sentence.Trēsyvēzos amīlōs and Amīlōs, Trēsyvēzos are equally valid, both "Son of the Sun, lead us."
The Vocative Particle AiWhen the vocative address trails the verb rather than leading it, the interjection Ai, "O," is placed directly before it, marking the phrase that follows as address rather than a trailing subject.Amīlōs Ai Trēsyvēzos, "Lead us, O Son of the Sun" (better formed than the bare Amīlōs Trēsyvēzos)
Verb, Object, and AddressA leading verb may take its object directly, before the vocative address closes the sentence, the address set off from the whole by a comma per the comma rule for clarifying context; per the Flexible Order rule, the whole may also invert, the address leading and the verb-object pair following, the same comma marking the boundary.Amīlōs vettiēr, Kardārys, "Teach us the law, Emperor." Equally, Trēsyvēzos, amīlōs vettiēr is a correct alternative to Amīlōs vettiēr, Trēsyvēzos, both "Teach us the law, Son of the Sun."

The Comma

RuleStatementExample
Serial ListingA comma separates each item in a list of proper nouns, verbs, or adjectives, so that each stands clearly defined rather than running together into an unbroken string of words.Trēsyvēzos, Gīmēperzys Nūmāzmēre, Zaldrīzēr Dorāzmēre
Clarifying ContextA comma also separates a leading verb from a vocative address that trails it, marking the boundary between the two and indicating the sentence's correct intent.Amīlōs, Trēsyvēzos is the grammatical form, the comma defining "Amīlōs" apart from "Trēsyvēzos."

Sentence-Final Punctuation

RuleStatementExample
The Full StopA full stop is placed at the end of a sentence.Amīlōs, Trēsyvēzos.
The Question MarkA question mark is placed at the end of a sentence if it is asking a question.Skorā? "Where?"
The Interrogative as a Complete SentenceSkorā, Skorī, Skorēl, Skorūt, Skorēd, and Skoron, each closed with a question mark, are considered proper sentences when the context is clear, communicating a response to a preceding statement.Skorā? Skorī? Skorēl? Skorūt? Skorēd? Skoron?

Demonstrative Suffixes

RuleStatementExample
This (-ēt)The suffix -ēt, added to the end of a noun, renders "this," pointing to a singular thing near at hand.Kardārys → Kardārysēt, "This Kardārys"
These (-ēti)The suffix -ēti, added to the end of a noun, renders "these," pointing to a plural of things near at hand.Raqiri → Raqiriēti, "These friends"
That (-āt)The suffix -āt, added to the end of a noun, renders "that," pointing to a singular thing at a remove.Prezīmos → Prezīmosāt, "That Division"
Those (-āti)The suffix -āti, added to the end of a noun, renders "those," pointing to a plural of things at a remove.Qrinuni → Qrinuniāti, "Those enemies"

The Full Glossary#

The glossary below is organized by grammatical function, then alphabetically within each: titles and epithets first (the bulk of the tongue's recorded vocabulary), then proper nouns, general nouns, adjectives, verbs, pronouns and grammar, numerals, and finally the tongue's interjections and set phrases.

Amīlen, "guiding," with ēli, "ones."

Giēñim-, "to heal," with the participle suffix -en and ēli, "ones."
Giesīrēligees-SEER-AY-lihHallowed OnesAn epithet of the Ēlvesēli used in rites and worship, naming them as set apart and made holy by their maker. Giesīr, "hallowed," fused to ēli, "ones."
Giesīrēliērigees-SEER-AY-lih-AY-rihThe Hallowed OnesGiesīrēli with the definite plural article -ēri fixed to the end of the whole fused word.
Gīmēperzys NūmāzmēreGEE-MAY-per-zihs NOO-MAHZ-MAY-rehBeacon of TruthAn honorific of the Vysoan throne: Gīmēperzys, "Beacon," and Nūmāzm, "Truth," carrying the definite article -ēr and the genitive -e ("of the Truth"); coined before the tongue's rules were settled as Gīmēperzys Nūmāzmēr, and brought into line with them. Adopted by Āeñāriōñ as the second member of his threefold style, and said ever since immediately after Trēsyvēzos.
Grozqirosgrohz-KIH-rohsMargraveLiterally "Companion of the Border"; held by a noble granted feudal tenure of a borderland by the Kardārys, with the duty of defending it.

GūrȳdrenēliGOO-REE-dreh-NAY-lihFate Bringing OnesThe Admonitors, the variant of the Ēlvesēli set between Morgharlax, the Stranger, and Drējegros, the Warrior: they offer warnings of conscience and rebukes against wrongdoing, counsel against continued straying, and deliver divine judgment. Hārvesqogror ValbartosHAHR-ves-koh-grohr VAHL-bahr-tohsCaptain 3rd ClassLiterally "Head Man of the 3rd Rank"; commanding officer of a Solsētegȳz, or executive officer of an Īligomēr.
Jaehēlēpēlyay-HAY-LAY-PAYLBreath Giver of God"The Breath Giver of God" or "the Animator of God." The spiritual being at the summit of the cosmological order beside the Jaehotāsīr, at parity with it but facing outward into creation: it animates the living, writes the natural law into the nature of things, quickens conscience and discernment, and leaves in every people an echo of the good. Taught in the Covenant's catechism.
Jaehotāsīryay-hoh-TAH-SEERThought of GodApproximately "Thought of God" or "God Thought." The spiritual being at the top of the cosmological order, just below the Starshaper: begotten from his very thought, the first to hear his thoughts, his foremost aide in the work of creation, and the being through whom he communes with the spiritual beings of the order and conveys his designs to them. Taught in the Covenant's catechism.
Jemīlenēliyeh-MEEL-eh-NAY-lihProtecting OnesThe Protectors, the variant of the Ēlvesēli set between Drējegros, the Warrior, and Vȳsēterys, the Smith: they defend the Starshaper's realm and his created worlds, safeguard his created beings, give them strength to choose right, and ward off evil. Jemīlen, "protecting," with ēli, "ones."

Jorrālionjentysyohr-RAH-lee-ohn-yen-tihsLieutenant CommanderLiterally "Placeholder Commander"; commanding officer of an Aderēbas or a Rāerēbas, or executive officer of a Solsētegȳz.
Jurnazantiyur-nah-ZAHN-tihSentinelsPlural of Jurnazantys.
Jurnazantysyur-nah-ZAHN-tihsSentinelMeaning "Watchful Knight"; the order's combat specialisation, guarding the Covenant's temples in peacetime, and its missions when they are sent, and standing beside the Kardārys in war.
Karadēmysēr Unavȳsōsekah-rah-DAY-mihs-AY-r oo-nah-VEE-sohsThe Sublime Throne of All-VysosThe full, formal name of the Vysoan state, carrying the definite article suffixed, -ēr, onto Karadēmys, the head noun, rather than onto Unavȳsōse, its genitive modifier.
Karāeksyskahr-AH-ek-sihsSublime LordA title of the Vysoan throne.
Karāeksys Unavȳsōsiikahr-AH-ek-sihs oo-nah-VEE-soh-see-eyeSublime Lord of All-VysoansNames the throne's claim to lordship over everyone who is Vysoan; added to the royal style by Vēzāeriōñ .
Kardārilaroskar-DAH-rih-lah-rohsImperial Crown PrinceLiterally "Great King's Heir"; the title of the Kardārys's heir, always his closest male relation.
Kardārilēsyñkar-DAH-rih-LAY-sihñImperial Crown PrincessThe feminine counterpart of Kardārilaros, built on the same root with the irregular formant -ēsyñ rather than the regular suffix -yñ. Held as a courtesy of marriage by the heir's spouse, and not retained should he predecease her.
Kardārlisoskar-DAHR-lih-sohsImperial PrinceLiterally "Great Little King"; held by any member of House Vēzgharyōñ at most four generations removed from a reigning Kardārys.
Kardārlisyñkar-DAHR-lih-sihñImperial PrincessThe feminine form of Kardārlisos, formed with the suffix -yñ.
Kardāryñkahr-DAHR-ihñEmpressThe feminine form of Kardārys; the style of his consort rather than of a woman reigning as sovereign in her own right. Stands outside the Sixteen Ranks exactly as Kardārys itself does. Presently held by Jaenanne Qelosiñe, consort to the reigning Āeñāriōñ .
Kardāryñārkahr-DAHR-ihñ-AHRThe EmpressKardāryñ with the definite article suffixed; after the feminine ending -yñ the suffix's vowel shifts to -ār rather than the tongue's usual -ēr.
Kardāryñikahr-DAHR-ihñ-ihEmpressesPlural of Kardāryñ, formed by the ordinary added -i.
Kardāryñiārikahr-DAHR-ihñ-ih-AH-rihThe EmpressesKardāryñi with the plural definite article suffixed, -āri, matching Kardāryñār's own shifted vowel.
Kardāryskahr-DAHR-ihsGreat King / High KingThe foremost title of the Vysoan throne, first claimed by Ēlyāegon ; interpretable also as "Emperor."
Kardārysērkahr-DAHR-ihs-AY-rThe KardārysKardārys with the definite article suffixed, -ēr, the tongue's productive rule for "the" in the singular — attached directly to the noun it marks rather than standing as a word of its own.
Kardrāzantyñkar-DRAH-zahn-tihñArchduchessThe feminine form of Kardrāzantys.
Kardrāzantyskar-DRAH-zahn-tihsArchdukeLiterally "Great Warrior-Lord" — the same Kar- prefix marking greatness already seen in Kardārys and Karadēmys, set before Drāzantys. Held by a noble whose house once ruled significant territory with vassals equivalent to a Lenqiros, and never granted outside the Imperial House.
Lenqiroslehn-KIH-rohsCountLiterally "Companion of the House"; held by a noble granted feudal tenure of a territory by the Kardārys.
Lenqiryñlehn-KIH-rihñCountessThe feminine form of Lenqiros.
MaegysdārMAY-gihs-DAHRWise LeaderThe title of an official holding a post in the Vysoan cabinet; better understood as Magister.
MaegysdāriMAY-gihs-DAH-rihWise LeadersPlural of Maegysdār.
MaegystīriMAY-gihs-TEE-rihCertified ScholarsPlural of Maegystīrys.
MaegystīrysMAY-gihs-TEE-rihsCertified ScholarLiterally "Wise One Attested"; the credential earned upon graduating a Maegysombāzmion.
MentiMEN-tihSoldiersPlural of Mentys.
MentysMEN-tihsSoldierThe base word for a single member of the Vysoan armed forces' enlisted rank and file; root of Ezīmenti and Tōmenti alike.
MēnybartosMAY-nih-bahr-tohsCorporalLiterally "Body Head"; may be appointed the specialist officer of a Lantēgrosi.
MīzantysMEE-zahn-tihsDefending WarriorThe shared root of both Mīzantys honorifics.
Mīzantys MaegysombāzmioneMEE-zahn-tihs may-gihs-ohm-BAHZ-mee-ohnDefender of the FortressLiterally "Defending Warrior of the Wise Man Fortress"; an honorific held by the head of House Vēzegsīdōr, granted for the close relationship the Vēzegsīdōri maintain with the Maegysombāzmioni.
Mīzantys PāsābarieMEE-zahn-tihs pah-SAH-bah-rihDefender of the FaithfulLiterally "Defending Warrior of the Faithful"; an honorific held by the Kardārys himself.
Oktiqirosohk-tih-KIH-rohsBurgraveLiterally "Companion of the City"; held by a noble granted feudal tenure of a fortified town by the Kardārys.
Oktiqiryñohk-tih-KIH-rihñBurgravineThe feminine form of Oktiqiros.
Ondoriēriohn-doh-rih-AY-rihThe PowersThe title of the highest orders among the Ēlvesēli. Ondori, the regular -or plural of a root Ondor, "Power," with the definite plural article -ēri.
PāleqirosPAH-leh-kih-rohsCount PalatineLiterally "Companion of the Crown"; held by a noble granted feudal tenure directly by the Kardārys of a territory larger than a Lenqiros's, usually of special significance to the crown.
PāleqiryñPAH-leh-kih-rihñCountess PalatineThe feminine form of Pāleqiros.
Pāsābariēripah-SAH-bah-rih-AY-rihThe FaithfulThe plural Pāsābari with the plural definite article suffixed, -ēri — "the adherents of the Sidereal Covenant," collectively.
Qelōgorloktyskeh-LOH-gohr-lohk-tihsSpacefarerLiterally "Starshipman"; leads a watch section of a ship's department.
Qeloktyskeh-LOHK-tihsAstronautLiterally "Astronaut."
Qīzy JenqēlosiKEE-zih yehn-KAY-loh-sihRear AdmiralLiterally "Supporting Commander of the Stars"; the rank of the officer who leads a Prezīmos.
QlādīlhārysKLAH-DEEL-HAH-rihsSergeantLiterally "Thrice Striped"; may be appointed the specialist officer of a Gāregrosi.
Qogrojentyskoh-groh-YEN-tihsColonelLiterally "Line Commander"; the rank of the officer who commands a Qogrokarysi.
RāelagonRAH-eh-lah-gohnKeeperA title for one who guards, cares for, or manages something.
Rāelagonēr NāmorghūlperzyseRAH-eh-lah-gohn-AY-r NAH-mor-GOOL-per-zihsKeeper of the Flame EternalNames the throne's role as benefactor and protector of the Sidereal Covenant, added to the royal style by Auriōñ ; carries the definite article suffixed, -ēr, onto Rāelagon, "Keeper," the head noun, rather than onto Nāmorghūlperzyse, its genitive modifier.
RāelenēliRAH-eh-leh-NAY-lihKeeping OnesThe Keepers, the variant of the Ēlvesēli set between Maegūryñ, the Crone, and Morgharlax, the Stranger: they record the works of the Starshaper, the events of his created worlds, the deeds of his creations, the secrets of the higher mysteries, and the ledger of good and evil. Built on Rāel-, "keep," as in Rāelagon, "Keeper," with the participle suffix -en and ēli, "ones."
RōvēzandārROH-VAY-zan-DAHRMajorLiterally "Great Warrior Lord"; the rank of the officer who commands a Grorzanti.
Rōvēzandār UndrāzmysROH-VAY-zan-DAHR oon-DRAHZ-mihsMajor GeneralLiterally "Great Warrior Lord General Commander"; the rank of the officer who commands a Ezīmenti.
SētegqēlosiērSAY-teg-KAY-loh-sih-AY-rThe StarshaperThe name of the god of the Sidereal Covenant: Sētegqēlosi, "Maker of the Stars" (Sēteg-, "to make," fused to qēlosi, "of the stars," the same way Jentys fuses to form Jenqēlosi, "Commander of the Stars"), with the definite article -ēr fixed to the whole word. Reserved for him alone, naming him as author of the stars rather than merely their servant or vessel, unlike the King's own borrowed cosmic epithets, Zirȳs Ñellenkaperzys and Gīmēperzys Nūmāzmēre.
SētegtīriSAY-teg-TEE-rihCertified CraftmastersPlural of Sētegtīrys.
SētegtīrysSAY-teg-TEE-rihsCertified CraftmasterLiterally "Made One Attested"; the credential earned upon graduating a Sētegombāzmion.
SēterenēliSAY-teh-reh-NAY-lihShaping OnesThe Artificers, the variant of the Ēlvesēli set between Vȳsēterys, the Smith, and Jēdkeporys, the Father: they assist the Starshaper in the act of creation, sub-creating according to his vision and inspiring his creations to do likewise. Sēter, "form, shape," with the participle suffix -en and ēli, "ones"; Sēter shares the old Valiērian root Sēte- with Sēteg-, "to make," in Sētegqēlosiēr.
TrēsyvēzosTRAY-sih-VAY-zohsSon of the SunAn honorific of the Vysoan throne; the first member of the threefold style adopted by Āeñāriōñ .
Tȳnves JorrālionTEEN-ves yohr-RAH-lee-ohn2nd LieutenantLiterally "Second Placeholder"; in the Army, assists an Ēlves Jorrālion; in the Navy, a ship's systems officer.
Tȳnvesqogror ValbartosTEEN-ves-koh-grohr VAHL-bahr-tohsCaptain 2nd ClassLiterally "Head Man of the 2nd Rank"; commanding officer of an Īligomēr, or executive officer of a Lōgorvīlībāze.
ŪbremenēliOO-breh-meh-NAY-lihTeaching OnesThe Teachers, the variant of the Ēlvesēli set between Arljēdryñ, the Maiden, and Maegūryñ, the Crone: they impart messages, and knowledge of truths, to the Starshaper's creations. Ūbremen, "teaching," with ēli, "ones."
Uēpajenongūrysoo-AY-pah-jen-ohn-GOO-rihsSenior Warrant OfficerLiterally "Old Leader by Knowledge"; may be appointed the specialist officer of a Mēnībāzmi (Army) or an Izulagror (Navy).
Uēpajenqeloktysioo-AY-pah-jehn-keh-lohk-tih-sihSenior Petty OfficerLiterally "Old Leader of Astronauts"; may be appointed the senior rating of a Lōgorvīlībāze or an Īligomēr.
Uēpamentysoo-AY-pah-men-tihsVeteran SoldierLiterally "Old Soldier."
Uēpaqeloktysoo-AY-pah-keh-lohk-tihsVeteran AstronautLiterally "Old Astronaut."
Uēpaqlādīlhārysoo-AY-pah-KLAH-DEEL-HAH-rihsSenior SergeantLiterally "Old Thrice Striped"; may be appointed the specialist officer of a Grorzanti.
Unañesīrātioo-nah-nyeh-SEER-AH-tihThose Before AllA liturgical and poetic epithet of the Ēlvesēli, who were made before all other creation; kept to hymn and invocation rather than ordinary speech. Una-, "all," joined to Ñesīr, "before," with the plural demonstrative suffix -āti, "those," standing as the noun.
ŪndissariOON-dih-sah-rihSeersPlural of Ūndissaros.
ŪndissarosOON-dih-sah-rohsSeerMeaning "Person of the Sight"; one who communes with the Starshaper and receives his will as prophecy, without interpreting it.
ŪndissaryñOON-dih-sah-rihñSeeressThe feminine form of Ūndissaros, formed with the tongue's regular suffix -yñ. Held by Kardārilēsyñ Elaenyra Ūndembreys, the one member of the immediate imperial family who stands a trained Solar Scion by right of her own gift of visions rather than by Vēzgharyōñ blood.
Undrāzmysoon-DRAHZ-mihsGeneralLiterally "General Commander"; the rank of the officer who commands a Kostōbazmi.
ValbartosVAHL-bahr-tohsCaptainLiterally "Head Man"; the rank of the officer who commands a Gāregrosi.
Valbartos JenqēlosiVAHL-bahr-tohs yehn-KAY-loh-sihCaptain AdmiralLiterally "Head Man Commander of the Stars"; the rank of the officer who leads a Giezbēvumptis.
Valbartos UndrāzmysVAHL-bahr-tohs oon-DRAHZ-mihsCaptain GeneralLiterally "Head Man General Commander"; the rank of the officer who commands a Grozostōbazmi.
Valzantyñvahl-ZAHN-tihñDameThe feminine form of Valzantys, formed with the suffix -yñ.
Valzantysvahl-ZAHN-tihsKnightLiterally "Warrior Man"; held by one granted the honour of knighthood, whether by merit or by induction into the Solar Scions.
VēzenkelariVAY-zen-keh-lah-rihSolar ScionsLiterally "Heirs of the Sun," rendered idiomatically as "Solar Scions."
VēzgharzantiVAYZ-gahr-ZAHN-tihSunblood SentinelsPlural of Vēzgharzantys.
VēzgharzantiēriVAYZ-gahr-ZAHN-tih-AY-rihThe Sunblood SentinelsVēzgharzanti with the plural definite article suffixed, -ēri, rather than the singular -ēr — the first attested case of the suffix's plural form, its -i echoing the same ending every other bare-r plural already takes.
VēzgharzantysVAYZ-gahr-ZAHN-tihsSunblood SentinelThe Kardārys's own bodyguard, drawn from among the Jurnazanti; takes the regular plural Vēzgharzanti.
VēzīrigomērVAY-ZEE-rih-goh-MAY-rOne Upon Whom the Sun SmilesLiterally "Sun Smiles Upon One"; an honorific granted by the Kardārys to those who have earned his greatest favour. Styled His or Her Radiance.
Zaldrāeksizahl-DRAH-ek-sihDragonlordsPlural of Zaldrāeksys; the forty ruling families of Valiērīa, who bonded their dragons through the gift.
Zaldrāeksyñzahl-DRAH-ek-sihñDragonladyThe feminine form of Zaldrāeksys.
Zaldrāeksyszahl-DRAH-ek-sihsDragonlordOne of the Zaldrāeksi, the dragon-bonded lords of Valiērīa; Zaldrīz, "Dragon," joined to Āeksys, "Lord."
Zaldrīzzahl-DREEZDragonThe bare root behind Zaldrīzēr Dorāzmēre, "The Dragon of the Void."
Zaldrīzēr Dorāzmērezahl-DREE-ZAY-r doh-RAHZ-MAY-rehThe Dragon of the VoidAn honorific of the Vysoan throne: Zaldrīz, "Dragon," and Dorāzm, "Void," each carrying the definite article -ēr, the genitive -e closing the second ("of the Void"). Coined before the tongue's rules were settled as Zaldrīzēr Dorāzmae, and brought into line with them; the third member of the threefold style adopted by Āeñāriōñ , said immediately after Gīmēperzys Nūmāzmēre.
Zirȳs Ñellenkaperzyszih-REES NYEL-len-kah-PER-zihsHe Who Is Fire Made FleshAn honorific of the Vysoan throne, added to the royal style by Baeriōñ .

Proper Nouns — Places, Peoples & Named Things

High VysoanPronunciationCommon VysoanMeaning
ĀedāriōñAH-eh-DAH-ree-OHNYSteadfast Ruler of LightA royal name of House Vēzgharyōñ, borne by Āedāriōñ , under whom the first hyperdrive was engineered.
ĀelyxanthorAH-eh-lihks-AN-thorIron Peace over PowerA royal name of House Vēzgharyōñ, built on Āegion, "Iron," Lyx, the archaic "Peace," Ana, "Over," and Thor, "Power"; borne by Āelyxanthor , the Navigator, Founder of the realm, and by Āelyxanthor .
ĀeñāriōñAH-eh-NYAH-ree-OHNYIron Risen in LightA royal name of House Vēzgharyōñ, built on Āegion, "Iron," Ñār, "Rising," and Iōñ, "of Light"; borne by Āeñāriōñ , Āeñāriōñ , and the reigning Āeñāriōñ .
ĀerakiiAH-eh-rah-kee-eyeAerakiiThe people of Āerakīs.
ĀerakīsAH-eh-rah-KEESAerakisA neighbouring realm folded into the crown's by the marriage of Āelyxanthor ; its people are the Āerakii.
ĀethelAH-eh-thelDestiny Made FirmA royal name of House Vēzgharyōñ, built on Āer, "Firm," its r dropped before Thel, "Destiny"; borne by no king to date, though by Prince Āethel, the only son of Kēlāeriōñ , killed by Sȳndorian raiders before he could reign.
Arloktionar-LOHK-tee-ohnNew TownA major city on South Ēlythoros's eastern coast.
AuriōñOW-ree-OHNYResplendent LightA royal name of House Vēzgharyōñ, built on Aurie, "Resplendent," and Iōñ, "of Light"; borne by Auriōñ , the Golden.
AuriōsOW-ree-OHSOur BrillianceA royal name of House Vēzgharyōñ, built on Aurie, "Brilliant"; borne by Auriōs , the Admirable.
AurysOW-rihsThe BrilliantA royal name of House Vēzgharyōñ, built on Aurie, "Brilliant," with the masculine ending -ys; borne by Aurys .
BaeriōñBAIR-ee-OHNYSummit of LightA royal name of House Vēzgharyōñ, built on Baer, "Summit," and Iōñ, "of Light"; borne by Baeriōñ , the Black.
BarBAHRHall, Gathering-placeA root naming the place where people gather, and by extension the gathering itself: it closes Gerialbar, "Meeting of the People," and opens Barsīvōñ, "Hall of Seven Lights."
Barsīvōñbahr-SEE-VOHNYHall of Seven LightsThe great temple of the Sidereal Covenant on the government island, raised by Āeñāriōñ and dedicated to the memory of Rāehaerys . Built on Bar, "Hall," Sīv, "Seven," and Ōñ, "Light."
Braedhōsbrayd-HOHSOur CopperA city state of Ñāqos that backed the thirteen-year revolt in Pelarton under Aurys , absorbed into the realm under Ēlyrōz , and later merged with Pelarton and two neighbouring cities into Dāervesālion.
DāeriōñDAH-eh-ree-OHNYLight UnboundA royal name of House Vēzgharyōñ, built on Dāer, "Unbound," and Iōñ, "of Light"; borne by Dāeriōñ , the Daring.
Dāervesāliondah-ehr-veh-SAH-lee-ohnLand of LibertyA single conurbation of Ñāqos, formed when the once-independent city states of Braedhōs and Pelarton merged with two of their neighbours. Built on Dāer, "Free."
DārilardōrDAH-rih-lar-DOHRPrince's FortA major city on North Ēlythoros's eastern coast, founded by Ēlythor while still a prince.
Dārliniondahr-LIH-nee-ohnKing's PortThe crown's second seat, at a great river's mouth in Endāros, grown from the union of three older towns.
ĒlyāegonAY-lih-AH-eh-gohnThe Iron OneA royal name of House Vēzgharyōñ, built on Āegion, "Iron"; borne by Ēlyāegon , the Enlightened, and by Ēlyāegon .
ĒlyrōzAY-lih-ROHZThe Renowned OneA royal name of House Vēzgharyōñ, built on Rōz, "Name"; borne by Ēlyrōz and by Ēlyrōz , the Erudite.
ĒlythelAY-lih-thelThe Destined OneA royal name of House Vēzgharyōñ, built on Thel, "Destiny"; borne by Ēlythel and by Ēlythel .
ĒlythorAY-lih-thorThe Mighty OneA royal name of House Vēzgharyōñ, built on Thor, "Power"; borne by Ēlythor , the Mariner.
ĒlythorosAY-lih-THOH-rohsElythorosThe continent discovered west of the Ēlythori isles by Prince Ēlythor, later King Ēlythor , the Mariner; later divided into North Ēlythoros and South Ēlythoros.
Endārosen-DAH-rohsEndarosThe westernmost of Vȳsōs's three anciently civilized continents.
Ghisazmagih-SAHZ-mahGhisazmaThe realm's shipbuilding heart, on the shores of a great bay in Ñāqos, grown from the union of three older cities.
Iōrvinionee-OHR-vih-nee-ohnCold HarbourA city on Rōvuēsos's southern tip, close to Zīrtos, raised to stage the Zīrtos expeditions.
Jemēsiñ Vēzoseyeh-MAY-sihñ VAY-zoh-sehAscension of the SunThe single Vēziñ set apart at the start of each Rȳarl, celebrated by the Vȳsōse as the turning of winter into spring.
Karjiōrionēr Ābrērkar-yih-OH-rih-ohn-AY-r AH-bray-rThe Great Hall of the PeopleThe domed hall on the government island raised by Āeñāriōñ , where both houses of the Gerialbar convene; the definite article, -ēr, is suffixed twice over in this compound — once onto Karjiōrion, the head noun, and again onto Ābre, its genitive modifier — marking "the Hall" and "the People" each as its own definite entity, rather than folding one suffix across the whole.
KēlāeriōñKAY-LAH-eh-ree-OHNYFirmament of LightA royal name of House Vēzgharyōñ, built on Kēlāer, "Firmament," and Iōñ, "of Light"; borne by Kēlāeriōñ , the Great.
KēlāeriōñarlKAY-LAH-eh-ree-OHNY-arlKēlāeriōñ CalendarThe Vysoan system of timekeeping, set down in the reign of Kēlāeriōñ in concert with the Eglābaros and the College of Jehābari, and unaltered since; it numbers its years from the birth of Āelyxanthor (see Rȳarl Ōsare Āeksys).
KēlāerysKAY-LAH-eh-rihsMan of the FirmamentA royal name of House Vēzgharyōñ, built on Kēlāer, "Firmament," with the masculine ending -ys; borne by Kēlāerys .
KēlāethorKAY-LAH-eh-thorPower of the FirmamentA royal name of House Vēzgharyōñ, built on Kēlāer, "Firmament," its r dropped before Thor, "Power"; borne by Kēlāethor .
Kēlinionkay-LIH-nee-ohnKelinionA major port city on Endāros's western coast.
MaegysdārarziēriMAY-gihs-DAHR-ar-zih-AY-rihThe MagistraciesThe fifteen office spires of the government island raised by Āeñāriōñ , one for each Magistracy the Qrogorjentys seats; scattered across the island rather than gathered upon the palace mount itself, they answer to no ceremonial precedence and so rise well past the mount's own tallest structure.
Merāeksysmehr-AH-ek-sihsMeraksesThe first planet in the Vēzos system.
Morghūlmor-GOOLMorghulThe seventh planet in the Vēzos system.
ÑāqosNYAH-kohsNyaqosThe easternmost of Vȳsōs's three anciently civilized continents.
Ñesīr ĀelyxanthorNYAY-seer AH-eh-lihks-AN-thorBefore ĀelyxanthorThe reckoning of years before the birth of Āelyxanthor , counted backward from it; abbreviated ÑĀ, as in ÑĀ 400.
Ōsar Vēzos Mazīl DaorOH-sar VAY-zohs mah-ZEEL DOWROur Sun Sets NotThe motto of House Vēzgharyōñ: Ōsar, "Our," Vēzos, "Sun," Mazīl, "to lie down, rest," and Daor, "Not"; the closing words of the Solar Scions' oath.
Pelartonpeh-LAR-tohnPelartonA city state of Ñāqos whose thirteen-year revolt, backed by Braedhōs, cost Aurys his life, and which Dāeriōñ brought to peace by negotiation; later merged into Dāervesālion.
Pryjatājoniprih-YAHT-ah-YOH-nihShattered IslandsThe island chain upon which Āelyxanthor , directed by the Starshaper, founded Zobrezos, the capital. Pryjat-, "Break," as in Pryjatsīr, "Shattered," joined to Ājoni, "Islands."
Qelendiekeh-LEN-dee-ehWestern GoldOne of the heartland cities of Sȳndorīa, absorbed into the realm in Vēzāeriōñ 's final war against it. Built on Qeld, "Gold."
RāehaerysRAH-eh-HAIR-ihsThe SteadfastA royal name of House Vēzgharyōñ, built on Rāehaer, "Constant," with the masculine ending -ys; borne by Rāehaerys , to whose memory the Barsīvōñ is dedicated.
RāeōñRAH-eh-OHNYKeeper of LightA royal name of House Vēzgharyōñ, built on Rāe, "Hold," and Ōñ, "Light"; borne by Rāeōñ .
RāethelRAH-eh-thelKeeper of DestinyA royal name of House Vēzgharyōñ, built on Rāe, "Hold," and Thel, "Destiny"; borne by Rāethel .
RāethorRAH-eh-thorKeeper of PowerA royal name of House Vēzgharyōñ, built on Rāe, "Hold," and Thor, "Power"; borne by Rāethor , the Restorer.
Rōvuēsosroh-voo-AY-sohsRovuesosThe southernmost of Vȳsōs's three anciently civilized continents.
Rȳarl Ōsare ĀeksysREE-arl OH-sah-reh AH-ek-sihsYear of Our LordThe era by which Vysoans reckon time, counted from the birth of Āelyxanthor : year 1 is the year of his birth, and there is no year 0. Abbreviated RŌĀ; the present year is RŌĀ 1017. Rȳarl, "Year," with Ōsar Āeksys, "Our Lord," the genitive -e falling on Ōsar alone (see The Genitive & Feminine Suffixes).
SȳndorīaSEEN-doh-REE-ahSyndoriaThe great rival realm against which the crown fought three wars: the first under Rāeōñ , which gained nothing; the second under Valkariōñ , won along with the peace; and the last under Vēzāeriōñ , who absorbed its heartland, Qelendie and Sȳndoval. Carries the suffix -rīa, "land of."
SȳndovalSEEN-doh-vahlShadow ManOne of the heartland cities of Sȳndorīa, absorbed into the realm in Vēzāeriōñ 's final war against it.
Taēsārtah-AY-SAHRTaesarThe second planet in the Vēzos system.
Tolmilentontohl-mih-LEN-tohnFar HomeThe main city of Ūlthos, founded under Rāethel .
ŪlthosOOL-thohsUlthosThe continent southeast of Ñāqos claimed for the crown under Rāethel for its abundance of rubber.
Udirēr Jaehoseoo-dih-RAY-r YAY-hoh-sehThe Word of GodThe Covenant's own holy book, upon which every oath of office is sworn; referred to colloquially as simply the Udirēr, "the Word."
Unavȳsōsoo-nah-VEE-sohsAll-VysosA name for the whole of Vȳsōs and, by extension, every territory under its sovereignty.
Unavȳsōsiioo-nah-VEE-soh-see-eyeAll-VysoansA collective title for everyone who is Vysoan; the All- form of Vȳsōsii.
VagusVAH-gussVagusThe sixth planet in the Vēzos system.
Valentonvah-LEN-tohnValentonOne of the largest of the city states that arose from the fall of Valiērīa, and the city in which Āelyxanthor began his life.
Valiērīavah-lee-AY-REE-ahLand of the Proven OnesOne of the oldest civilizations of early Vȳsōs, ruled by the Zaldrāeksi of forty families; it grew from a city state into an empire and endured for thousands of years, until its capital and core were destroyed in the Cataclysm. House Vēzgharyōñ was among the few to survive. Shares its root with Valiēre, "of the Proven," with the suffix -rīa, "land of."
Valiēriivah-lee-AY-ree-eyeValiēriansThe people of Valiērīa.
Valkariōñvahl-KAH-ree-OHNYExalted in LightA royal name of House Vēzgharyōñ, built with Iōñ, "of Light"; borne by Valkariōñ , the Venerable, Valkariōñ , and Valkariōñ .
Valkarōzvahl-kah-ROHZExalted NameA royal name of House Vēzgharyōñ, built on Rōz, "Name"; borne by Valkarōz .
Valkarysvahl-KAH-rihsThe ExaltedA royal name of House Vēzgharyōñ, with the masculine ending -ys; borne by Valkarys and by Valkarys .
Vējōzosvay-YOH-zohsSouthern SunThe great city of the realm's south, founded on the coast of Rōvuēsos in Kēlāerys 's reign, its name echoing the capital's own on purpose.
Vermitosvur-MIH-tohsVermitosThe fifth planet in the Vēzos system.
VēzāelyxVAY-ZAH-eh-lihksPeace of the Enduring SunA royal name of House Vēzgharyōñ, built on Vēzos, "Sun," Āer, "Enduring," and Lyx, the archaic "Peace"; borne by Vēzāelyx .
VēzāeriōñVAY-ZAH-eh-ree-OHNYLight of the Enduring SunA royal name of House Vēzgharyōñ, built on Vēzos, "Sun," Āer, "Enduring," and Iōñ, "of Light"; borne by Vēzāeriōñ , the Magnificent, and by Vēzāeriōñ , the Stargazer.
VēzāerysVAY-ZAH-eh-rihsMan of the Enduring SunA royal name of House Vēzgharyōñ, built on Vēzos, "Sun," and Āer, "Enduring," with the masculine ending -ys; borne by Vēzāerys , Vēzāerys , and Vēzāerys .
VēzāethorVAY-ZAH-eh-thorPower of the Enduring SunA royal name of House Vēzgharyōñ, built on Vēzos, "Sun," Āer, "Enduring," its r dropped before Thor, "Power"; borne by Vēzāethor .
Vēzegsīdōrvay-zeg-SEE-DOHRHouse VēzegsīdōrThe noble house founded by a younger son of Ēlyrōz married into the ancient tower-keepers of Uēpoktio, which has held the stewardship of the Maegysombāzmion since and maintains a close relationship with the Maegysombāzmioni, holding the honorific Mīzantys Maegysombāzmione for it.
VēzinītsosVAY-zih-NEE-tsohsSun RestA major city on North Ēlythoros's western coast.
VēzosVAY-zohsVezosThe star of the Vēzos system.
VēzperzyonVAYZ-per-zih-OHNVezperzyonThe third planet in the Vēzos system, home to the realm's one small colony, established under Vēzāerys .
VēzqeldeVAYZ-kel-dehGold of the SunThe Vysoan currency, the Vēzos system's own legal tender by the throne's prerogative; digital in ordinary use by RŌĀ 1017, though backed still by the crown's own physical gold reserves. Written under the code VĒQ. Built on Qeld, "Gold."
VȳsōmēdonVEE-SOH-MAY-donVysos's SteelAn alloy worked from Adamant ore by a method the crown keeps a closely guarded secret; used to forge the sunblade issued to every Scion upon initiation, and Brightflame, the Kardārys's own blade.
VȳsōsVEE-sohsVysosThe fourth planet in the Vēzos system — the homeworld of the Vysoans and the seat of House Vēzgharyōñ.
VȳsōsiiVEE-soh-see-eyeVysoansThe plural of Vȳsōse, drawn down from the archaic Vȳsōsei; the people of the planet Vȳsōs, or of its culture and species wherever found.
ZīrtosZEER-tohsZirtosThe polar continent to the far south, sighted and charted under Kēlāerys and formally claimed under Valkarys .

Nouns

High VysoanPronunciationCommon VysoanMeaning
Aderēbasah-deh-RAY-bahsCorvetteLiterally "Fast Traveller"; the lighter of the Vysoan Navy's two Escort patterns, and the smallest class of starship it fields.
ĀegionAH-eh-gee-ohnIronA noun for iron; the root behind the royal names Ēlyāegon, "The Iron One," and Āeñāriōñ, "Iron Risen in Light."
Āekyñissah-EH-kih-ñihsLadyshipThe feminine counterpart of Āekysiss, "Lordship," formed by the tongue's own -yñ feminine suffix replacing the masculine ending outright, exactly as it does in Kardāryñ.
Āekysissah-EH-kih-SIHSLordshipLiterally "the condition of being a lord"; shares its Āekys- root with Āeksiōrion, the Gerialbar's noble upper house, and takes the abstract-condition suffix -iss (compare Egliss, Vaoriss, Āekyñiss).
ĀjonAH-yohnIslandA noun for an island; plural Ājoni.
ĀjoniAH-yoh-nihIslandsPlural of Ājon, formed by the Additive Class; the second element of Pryjatājoni, "Shattered Islands."
Anarōveglissah-nah-ROH-veh-glihsSublimityLiterally "in the condition of great height over all"; the prefix ana-, "over" or "throughout" (compare Anaqēlosi, Anavȳsōs), set before Rōvegliss, "Majesty." The style proper to Sētegqēlosiēr, the Starshaper, alone, standing one degree above the Kardārys's own Rōvegliss, as Rōvegliss stands above Egliss. The Kar- prefix that renders "sublime" in Karāeksys and Karadēmys is barred to him by the Rule of Reservation, which holds Kar- to House Vēzgharyōñ and its throne.
Arlēdar-LAYDHourOne twenty-fourth of a Vēziñ, holding sixty Bykēdi.
Arlentrotahr-LEN-trohtNew HouseA noun naming a house of the low nobility. Compare Eglentrot and Lentrot.
Arliegūrēnar-lih-eh-GOO-RAYNInnovationLiterally "New Knowledge"; the Magistracy responsible for research and development.
BaerBAIRPoint, TipA point or tip, used also to mean a summit or apex; root of the royal name Baeriōñ, "Summit of Light."
Baldorāzbahl-doh-RAHZBlack HoleLiterally "Black Void"; the standard name for a black hole. Bal, "Black," joined to Dorāzm, "Void," whose final m drops in the compound, by the tongue's habit of shedding a final non-vowel.
BēvumptisBAY-voomp-tihsFleetLiterally "To Hover"; a numbered fleet, the Navy's principal formation, defined by the role it is given rather than by any fixed count of hulls.
Botȳsgūrēñionboh-TEES-goo-RAY-nyee-ohnTrade Learning HallThe pathway institution (ages 16–20) training essential trade skills through guild-sponsored apprenticeship, alongside social sciences, craft and performance aesthetics, Personal Formation, and applied technologies; the practical counterpart to the Otāgūrēñion.
Botȳsgūrēñioniboh-TEES-goo-RAY-nyee-oh-neeTrade Learning HallsPlural of Botȳsgūrēñion.
Botȳsombāzmionboh-TEES-om-BAHZ-mee-ohnThe Trade AcademyGathered body of trade; a tertiary technical trade school training starship systems, mining and colony engineering, navigation, and piloting — sharing its Botȳs- root, "Trade," with the Botȳsgūrēñion whose leavers it is chiefly built to take in.
Botȳsombāzmioniboh-TEES-om-BAHZ-mee-oh-neeTrade AcademiesPlural of Botȳsombāzmion.
Bykabēvumptisbih-kah-BAY-voomp-tihsFlotillaLiterally "Little To Hover"; the smallest grouping of vessels sailing together under a single commander.
Bykēdbih-KAYDMinuteOne sixtieth of an Arlēd, dividing further into a thousand Pyrysēdi.
Dohaeriridoh-HAI-rih-rihServantsPlural of Dohaeriros, formed by the Drop-and-Replace rule for a noun ending -os.
Dohaeririedoh-HAI-rih-rihServants ofGenitive plural of Dohaeriri, formed with the tongue's own -e genitive suffix; pronounced identically to the plain plural, the case carried in spelling alone.
Dohaerirosdoh-HAI-rih-rohsServantOne who serves in a household, common or noble alike; a general term, not a rank or office of its own.
Dorāzmdoh-RAHZMVoidThe bare root behind Zaldrīzēr Dorāzmēre, "The Dragon of the Void," and the second element of Baldorāz.
ĒdruryñAY-droo-rihñDreamA noun naming the mind's vision in sleep; its bare root Ēdrur stands alone as the second element of Gaēdrur, "Would, hypothetical action."
Eglentroteh-GLEN-trohtHigh HouseA noun naming a house of the high nobility. Compare Vēzghare Eglentrot, Lentrot, and Arlentrot.
EglissEG-lihsHighnessLiterally "in the condition of height"; shares the root Egl-, "high," with Eglentrot, "High House," and Egliñ, "Noble," and takes the abstract-condition suffix -iss (compare Āekysiss, Āekyñiss, Vaoriss).
Gadrējesgah-DRAY-yessShould, Right ActionGa, "Act," joined to Drējes, "right, true, correct," here in its complete suffix form, retaining the final -s; names the action that ought to be done.
Gaēdrurgah-AY-droorWould, Hypothetical ActionGa, "Act," joined to Ēdrur, the bare root behind Ēdruryñ, "Dream"; names an action held only in supposition.
Gakelingah-KEH-lihnCould, Possible ActionGa, "Act," joined to Kelin, "Chance, or Possible"; names an action that might be done.
Gaomagorgow-MAH-gorAgencyAn institution devoted to gathering knowledge the throne does not advertise publicly; two presently sit the Qrogorjentys alongside its fifteen Magistracies.
Gaomagorigow-mah-GOH-rihAgenciesPlural of Gaomagor.
GēlierGAY-lee-ehrSilverA noun for silver.
Gerialbargeh-ree-AL-barMeeting of the PeopleBuilt on Bar, "Hall," the place of gathering. Vȳsōs's legislature as a whole, sitting as two houses: the Āeksiōrion above and the Qupteōrion (Common Hall) below.
Giezbēvumptisgeez-BAY-voomp-tihsSystem FleetLiterally "Whole Arrangement To Hover"; the whole of the Vysoan Navy, taken together under one command.
GūrēñilaksiGOO-RAY-nyih-lahk-sihDiscovery of SecretsThe shared head-word carried by both Gaomagori's names.
Gūrēñilaksi LendārionGOO-RAY-nyih-lahk-sih len-DAH-ree-ohnDomestic IntelligenceLiterally "Discovery of Secrets at Home"; the Agency responsible for intelligence within Vysoan space.
Gūrēñilaksi NaeqēlosieGOO-RAY-nyih-lahk-sih nay-KAY-loh-sihGalactic IntelligenceLiterally "Discovery of Secrets of Many Stars"; the Agency charged with watching what lies beyond the Vēzos system as the realm enters the galaxy.
GūrotGOO-rohtFateFate in the sense of deserved fate: what a soul has earned, as distinct from fate merely suffered. Joined with Ȳdra to form Gūrȳdr-, "to announce deserved fate."
HūrarlHOO-rarlMonthLiterally "Moon Change"; a span of four Sīkōzi, twenty-eight Vēziñi in all.
ĪligomērEE-lih-goh-MAY-rCruiserLiterally "One That Crosses."
Iōñee-OHNYof LightInterchangeable with Yōñ, "of Light"; the form that survives in the royal names Auriōñ, Baeriōñ, Dāeriōñ, Kēlāeriōñ, Valkariōñ, and Vēzāeriōñ.
ĪtsgūrēñionEETS-goo-RAY-nyee-ohnLittle Learning HallThe foundational institution (ages 5–15) every subject of the throne passes through, noble and common alike; shares its gūrēñion root, "Learning Hall," with the Otāgūrēñion and Botȳsgūrēñion that follow it.
ĪtsgūrēñioniEETS-goo-RAY-nyee-oh-neeLittle Learning HallsPlural of Ītsgūrēñion.
Izūgadaororih-ZOO-gah-dah-oh-rohrDreadnoughtLiterally "To Fear Nothing"; the lesser of the Vysoan Navy's two Dreadnought patterns. Compare Karizūgadaoror.
Izulagrorih-zoo-LAH-grohrSquadronLiterally "Group of Four"; a grouping of divisions within a numbered fleet.
JāelāeksioYAH-eh-lah-AH-ek-see-ohTreasuryLiterally "to Store Gold"; the Magistracy responsible for the crown's finances.
Jemīlēlyeh-MEEL-AYLProtectorOne who protects: Jemīl-, "protect," with the agent suffix -ēl.
Jemīlēliyeh-MEEL-AY-lihProtectorsPlural of Jemīlēl, "Protector," formed with -ēli.
Kardārōñe Qogrorāzma Vēzenkelariekahr-DAH-ROH-nyeh koh-groh-RAHZ-mah VAY-zen-keh-lah-rihThe Imperial Military Order of the Solar ScionsThe chivalric order of the gifted, grown from the seers of the flame and established as a standing crown institution by Kēlāeriōñ , its rule, branches, dress and oath codified by Valkarōz ; de jure under the Eglābaros's jurisdiction as head of the Covenant, de facto commanded, led, and managed by the Kardārys in his own role as Jentys Pāsābarie. Its oath closes with the house's motto, Ōsar Vēzos Mazīl Daor.
Kardārōñe Qrogorjentyskahr-DAH-ROH-nyeh kroh-gor-YEN-tihsThe Imperial Group of LeadersThe Cabinet's full, formal name, used in any document of state.
Karizūgadaororkahr-ih-ZOO-gah-dah-oh-rohrDreadnought (great pattern)Literally "Great To Fear Nothing"; the greater of the Vysoan Navy's two Dreadnought patterns, the largest class of starship it designs. Compare Izūgadaoror.
KēlKAYLAetherA noun for the aether; root of Kēlāer, "Firmament."
KēlāerKAY-LAH-ehrFirmamentKēl, "Aether," joined to Āer, "Firm"; the root behind the royal names Kēlāeriōñ, Kēlāerys, and Kēlāethor.
KelinKEH-lihnChance, Or PossibleBoth noun and adjective, as Vȳsōse is both noun and adjective: a chance or possibility, and, of a thing, "possible"; the root behind Kelindaor and Gakelin.
Kelindaorkeh-LIHN-dowrNo Chance, Or ImpossibleKelin, "Chance, or Possible," with Daor, "Not," suffixed; the negated form, again serving as both noun and adjective.
Lendārionlen-DAH-ree-ohnHomeland AffairsLiterally "Home Kingdom"; the Magistracy responsible for domestic governance.
LentrotLEN-trohtHouseA noun naming a house of the nobility generally. Compare Eglentrot and Arlentrot.
LōgorvīlībāzeLOH-gohr-VEE-LEE-BAH-zehBattleshipLiterally "Ship of Battle."
LyksLIHKSPeaceA noun for peace, in its modern spelling; compare the archaic Lyx.
LyxLIHKSPeaceThe archaic spelling of Lyks, "Peace," kept in the royal names Āelyxanthor and Vēzāelyx.
Maegūrōñosmay-GOO-ROH-nyohsEnlightenmentLiterally "Wise Knowledge Light"; the Magistracy responsible for education and spiritual instruction.
MaegysdārarziMAY-gihs-DAHR-ar-zihMagistraciesPlural of Maegysdārarz.
MaegysdārarzMAY-gihs-DAHR-arzMagistracyThe institution led by a Maegysdār; one of the fifteen bodies that together handle every core function of Vysoan governance.
Maegysombāzmionmay-gihs-ohm-BAHZ-mee-ohnthe FortressLiterally "Wise Man Fortress"; the ancient fortress at Uēpoktio, given its name by Ēlyrōz , the Erudite, upon completing its renovation into the realm's first Maegysombāzmion and one of its genuine centers of learning, and the seat of House Vēzegsīdōr's stewardship since.
MaegysombāzmionMAY-gihs-om-BAHZ-mee-ohnThe FortressGathered body of the wise; a tertiary academic institution training law, medicine, engineering theory, theology, and magistracy administration. The name of the fortress at Uēpoktio, first renovated and founded to that purpose under Ēlyrōz ; generalized in the centuries since to any comparable institution raised elsewhere across Vȳsōs.
Maegysombāzmionimay-gihs-ohm-BAHZ-mee-oh-neeFortressesPlural of Maegysombāzmion.
MīsesīrvīlībāzMEE-seh-SEER-VEE-LEE-BAHZDefence and WarLiterally "to Defend and War"; the Magistracy responsible for the Vysoan military.
Naenierēbanay-nee-eh-RAY-bahTransportLiterally "Many to Travel"; the Magistracy responsible for transit and infrastructure.
Naeqēlmoninay-KAYL-moh-nihGalactic AffairsLiterally "Many Stars Choices"; the Magistracy charged with the realm's relations beyond Vȳsōs, and with preparing for the day it first meets another civilization among the stars.
NāmorghūlperzysNAH-mor-GOOL-per-zihsThe Flame EternalA name for the light of the Starshaper, and for his devotees.
ŌñOHNYLightLight, as sunlight or starlight; the root of Ōñēr, "The Light," of Barsīvōñ, "Hall of Seven Lights," and of the archaic genitive Yōñ, "of Light."
OndorOHN-dorPowerA noun for power; root of Ondoriēri, "The Powers." Its archaic spelling Onthor gives the combining form Thor.
Ōñēroh-NYAY-rThe LightBuilt on the root Ōñ, "Light," with the definite article suffix -ēr already fixed to it; first attested in the royal liturgy.
OnthorOHN-thorPowerThe archaic spelling of Ondor, "Power," and the source of the combining form Thor.
Otāgūrēñionoh-TAH-goo-RAY-nyee-ohnThinking Learning HallThe pathway institution (ages 16–20) training philosophy, rhetoric, and social sciences alongside aesthetics theory and Personal Formation; the preparatory grounding a Maegysombāzmion's own education presumes of most who arrive at its gates, though a Botȳsgūrēñion leaver of sufficient aptitude and disposition may enter by that gate as well.
Otāgūrēñionioh-TAH-goo-RAY-nyee-oh-neeThinking Learning HallsPlural of Otāgūrēñion.
Prezīmospreh-ZEE-mohsDivisionLiterally "To be Divided"; a grouping of flotillas within a squadron.
Pyrysēdpih-rih-SAYDInstantLiterally "Thousand Times"; one thousandth of a Bykēd, the smallest unit of Vysoan timekeeping in ordinary use.
QeldKELDGoldA noun for gold; root of Vēzqelde, "Gold of the Sun," and Qelendie, "Western Gold."
Qogrorāzmakoh-groh-RAHZ-mahGroup CommandA compound word translated literally as "Group Command," but best understood as referring to a militarized order of chivalry.
QrinunKREE-nuhnEnemyA noun for an enemy or foe; the root behind the adjective Qrinunkes, "Hostile."
Qrogorjentyskroh-gor-YEN-tihsGroup of LeadersThe short, working name of the Vysoan Cabinet.
Qupteōrionkoop-teh-OH-ree-ohnCommon HallThe lower house of the Gerialbar, where the realm's own commons sit, checked from above by the noble Āeksiōrion; the same pairing repeats at every one of the Five Governances' own tiers.
RāerēbasRAH-eh-RAY-bahsTransportLiterally "Traveller That Holds," from Rāe, "Hold," and -rēbas, "traveller," as in Aderēbas; the Vysoan Navy's Transport class, carrying troops, cargo, and colonists rather than standing in the line of battle or among its Escort patterns.
RaqirRAH-kihrFriendA noun for a friend; plural Raqiri.
Raqirirah-KEE-rihFriendsPlural of Raqir, formed by the tongue's own added-i rule for a noun ending in bare -r.
RīglesREE-glehsHonourA noun for honour, standing as its own root; compare the derived adjective Rīglekosta, "Honorable."
RōveglissROH-veh-glihsMajestyLiterally "in the condition of great height"; built on Egliss, "Highness," with an intensifying element expressing greatness, the style proper to the Kardārys and Kardāryñ alone.
RȳarlREE-arlYearA span of thirteen Hūrarli and one further Vēziñ, that extra day set apart at the year's very start as the Jemēsiñ Vēzose.
SētegombāzmionSAY-teg-om-BAHZ-mee-ohnThe GuildhallGathered body of the made; a tertiary vocational college training guild-mastery in metallurgy, shipwrighting, textile work, and agricultural management.
SētegombāzmioniSAY-teg-om-BAHZ-mee-oh-neeGuildhallsPlural of Sētegombāzmion.
SētegsȳziSAY-teg-SEE-zihIndustryLiterally "to Make Goods"; the Magistracy responsible for manufacturing.
SēterSAY-terForm, ShapeFrom the older High Valiērian Sēterys. Shares the old Valiērian root Sēte- with Sēteg-, "to make"; root of Sēterenēli, "Shaping Ones."
Sīkōzsee-KOHZWeekLiterally "Seven Dawns"; a span of seven Vēziñi.
Sindisīrliorasihn-dih-SEER-lee-oh-rahTradeLiterally "to Buy and to Sell"; the Magistracy responsible for commerce.
Solsētegȳzsohl-SAY-teh-GEEZFrigateLiterally "Made to Sail"; the heavier of the Vysoan Navy's two Escort patterns.
ThelTHELMeaning, PurposeA noun for meaning, purpose, or destiny; root of the royal names Āethel, Ēlythel, and Rāethel.
ThorTHORPowerThe combining form of "Power," derived from Onthor, the archaic spelling of Ondor; it closes the royal names Āelyxanthor, Ēlythor, Kēlāethor, Rāethor, and Vēzāethor.
ŪbremagīsOO-breh-mah-GEESCultureLiterally "Tending the Soul"; the Magistracy responsible for the realm's arts and heritage.
Valarsȳrīvah-lar-SEE-REEHealthLiterally "All-Men Well"; the Magistracy responsible for public health and medicine.
VāldVAHLDTreeA noun for a tree, standing as its own root. Its final -d keeps it distinct from Val-, "man," as in Valbartos; the definite article attaches directly, Vāldēr, "the Tree," and its plural is Vāldi, after Bykēd and Bykēdi. Root of Vāld Sētere, "Tree of Creation."
Valkustikovahl-koos-TIH-kohManpowerLiterally "Man Strength"; the Magistracy responsible for labour and the workforce.
Vaorissvah-OH-rihsGraceLiterally "in the condition of favor"; built with the abstract-condition suffix -iss (compare Egliss, Āekysiss, Āekyñiss) on a root meaning "favor."
Vēdrogarvay-DROH-gahrRageA noun for consuming fury; first attested in the royal liturgy, where it opens the invocation Vēdrogar Vȳsōs and joins Zālar to form Vēdrogar Zālar, "Burning Rage."
Vēdrogar Zālarvay-DROH-gahr ZAH-lahrBurning RageA set phrase from the royal liturgy, joining Vēdrogar, "Rage," and Zālar, "Burn."
VēdrosVAY-drohsAngerA noun for anger, sharing its root with Vēdrogar, "Rage"; first attested in the royal liturgy, called twice in succession, Vēdros, Vēdros.
VettsīrdārdrīvoVETT-SEER-DAHR-DREE-vohLaws and JusticeLiterally "Laws and King's Justice"; the Magistracy responsible for the realm's legal code and its enforcement.
Vēzghare EglentrotVAYZ-gah-reh eh-GLEN-trohtHigh House of the Sun-BloodA noun naming a house of the sun-blood, set above Eglentrot itself in rank and reserved for kin of the throne.
VēziñVAY-zihñDayLiterally "Sun Birth"; the Vysoan day, holding twenty-four Arlēdi, reckoned under the Kēlāeriōñ Calendar.
VēzkostioVAYZ-kohs-tee-ohEnergyLiterally "Sun Power"; the Magistracy responsible for power generation.
Vēzȳndosvay-ZEEN-dohsShadow SunFirst attested in the royal liturgy, called alone in triples as a refrain.
VȳsVEESGroundThe bound root behind the planet's own name, Vȳsōs (built with the old suffix -ōs, "world" or "shine"), recorded also as a free word in its own right, meaning simply "ground." A common noun, lower-cased in running prose as vȳs — the headword above is shown capitalized only by the glossary's own display convention.
VȳsegorāeksioVEE-seh-goh-RAH-ek-see-ohNatural ResourcesLiterally "World Lands Gold"; the Magistracy responsible for the realm's raw materials.
VȳsērVEES-AY-rThe Groundvȳs, "ground," with the definite article suffixed, -ēr, attaching directly since the root already ends in a consonant with nothing to elide. It stays distinct in spelling from Vȳsōsēr, "The Vysoan" (see the Adjectives table below).
VȳsiēriVEES-ee-AY-rihThe Groundsvȳs with a plural -i, then the plural definite article -ēri — a simple added -i rather than the -os-dropping class Kardārys and Jehābaros follow, exactly as given.
YōñYOHNYof LightThe archaic genitive of Ōñ, "Light," from the time when e-, y- or i- was set before a word to mark "of"; interchangeable with Iōñ. Joined to a word ending in a vowel, it takes an r before it, as in Āeñāriōñ.
ZūgerZOO-gehrFearServes both as the plain noun and as an imperative, "Fear [it]"; first attested in the royal liturgy's refrain Zūger Ōñēr Vēzose, "Fear the Light of Vēzos," repeated four times in succession.

Adjectives

High VysoanPronunciationCommon VysoanMeaning
ĀerAH-ehrFirm, EnduringDerived from Āegion, "Iron," the firm metal, which is why the two sound alike and why a name's Āe- may be read as either. An h is added before it when joined to a word ending in a vowel, as in Rāehaer, "Constant"; its r drops before a suffix beginning with a non-vowel, as in Āethel and Kēlāethor.
Anaqēlosiah-nah-KAY-loh-sihOver the StarsThe same prefix ana- joined to qēlosi, "stars," the prefix itself supplying the relation (compare Naeqēlosie, "of Many Stars"); used of the King's dominion reaching beyond Vysos itself.
Anarȳarlah-nah-REE-arlThrough All the YearsAna- joined to Rȳarl, "year"; an expression of permanence used of the crown and the Flame Eternal alike, rendered idiomatically as "forever."
Anavȳsōsah-nah-VEE-sohsOver VysosAn honorific modifier naming dominion over Vysos itself, formed with the prefix ana-, "over" or "throughout," paired with the older Una-, "all"; first attested in the royal liturgy.
Arlēkesar-LAY-kessHourlyBuilt on Arlēd, "Hour," with the tongue's -kes suffix; the root's final non-vowel -d is dropped before the suffix is added to the remaining vowel.
AurieOW-ree-ehBrilliant, ResplendentBrilliant, resplendent, or shining; root of the royal names Auriōñ, Auriōs, and Aurys.
BalBAHLBlackThe colour black; as a prefix it marks a thing as black, as in Baldorāz, "Black Void."
DāerDAH-ehrFree, UnboundRoot of the royal name Dāeriōñ, "Light Unbound," and of Dāervesālion, "Land of Liberty."
DārykesDAHR-ih-kessKinglyAn adjective built on Dārys, "King," with the tongue's -kes suffix.
EgliñEG-lihñNobleLiterally "Highborn"; shares the root Egl-, "high," with Eglentrot, "High House," and Egliss, "Highness"; the style Noble Grace, held by an Archduke or Archduchess.
ĒlvalykesAYL-vah-lih-kessPrincelyAn adjective built on Ēlvalys, "Prince," with the -kes suffix.
GareGAH-rehSanguineLiterally "of Blood"; shares its root with Kardārōgar, "of the Great Royal Blood," the style Sanguine Highness held by a Prince or Princess of the Blood.
HūrakesHOO-rah-kessMonthlyBuilt on Hūrarl, "Month," with the tongue's -kes suffix; both trailing non-vowels of -rl are dropped before the suffix is added to the remaining vowel, per the general rule.
Kardārōgarkar-DAH-ROH-garof the Great Royal BloodA modifier marking descent from a reigning Kardārys; paired with Dārlisos or Dārlisyñ, in the inflected form Kardārōgare, to name a Prince or Princess of the Blood (Dārlisos Kardārōgare, Dārlisyñ Kardārōgare).
Kardārōñekahr-DAH-ROH-nyehImperialA term derived from the throne's own title; best translated as "Imperial."
Kardārōñērkahr-DAH-ROH-ny-AY-rThe ImperialKardārōñe with the definite article suffixed, -ēr, its own final -e elided before the suffix exactly as Vȳsōsēr's was.
Kardārōñikahr-DAH-ROH-nihImperialsPlural of Kardārōñe — the first attested case of a noun ending in a bare -e taking the drop-and-replace plural pattern otherwise reserved for -ys and -os, its own final -e dropped for a bare -i in the same way.
Kardārōñiērikahr-DAH-ROH-nih-AY-rihThe ImperialsKardārōñi with the plural definite article suffixed, -ēri.
Kardārykeskahr-DAHR-ih-kessImperiallyBuilt on Kardārys, "Great King," with the -kes suffix.
LykaeLIH-kaiSereneLiterally "of Calm"; the style Serene Highness, held by a Prince or Princess of the high nobility.
Maegykesmay-GEE-kessWiselyBuilt on Maegys, "Wise," with the -kes suffix.
MaegysMAY-gihsWiseThe bare adjectival root behind Maegysdār, Maegysombāzmion, and the tongue's other "wise" compounds, also standing as a word in its own right.
Naeqēlosienay-KAY-loh-sihof Many StarsThe genitive of Naeqēlosi, "Many Stars," the same root behind Naeqēlmoni; formed with the -e suffix as Dohaeririe is from Dohaeriri, and pronounced as the plain plural, the case carried in spelling alone.
ÑārNYAHRRisingRoot of the middle element of the royal name Āeñāriōñ, "Iron Risen in Light."
Qrinukeskrih-NOO-kessHostileBuilt on Qrinun, "Enemy," with the tongue's -kes suffix; the root's final non-vowel -n is dropped before the suffix is added to the remaining vowel.
Raqikesrah-KEE-kessFriendlyBuilt on Raqir, "Friend," with the -kes suffix.
RīglekostaREE-gleh-KOHS-tahHonorableLiterally "able to honor"; built on Rīgles, "Honour," with the suffix -kosta expressing ability, "able to"; the style Honourable Lordship or Ladyship, held by a Margrave/Margravine or Burgrave/Burgravine.
RōkesROH-kessNamelyBuilt on Rō-, "Name," with the -kes suffix; the root ends in a vowel, so -kes attaches directly, per the general rule.
RōkesīrROH-kes-EERSo NamedBuilt on Rōkes, "Namely," with the perfective suffix -sīr; the suffix's own leading s merges into the root's trailing -s (Rōkes + -sīr → Rōkesīr), but the suffix's macroned -ī is never elided or shortened — -sīr always keeps its long ī, whatever precedes it — giving a resultative sense, "so named" or "thus called."
RȳakesREE-ah-kessYearlyBuilt on Rȳarl, "Year," with the tongue's -kes suffix; both trailing non-vowels of -rl are dropped before the suffix is added to the remaining vowel, per the general rule.
Sīkōkessee-KOH-kessWeeklyBuilt on Sīkōz, "Week," with the tongue's -kes suffix; the root's final non-vowel -z is dropped before the suffix is added to the remaining vowel.
Valiērevah-lee-AY-rehof the ProvenThe genitive form behind Valiērīa, "Land of the Proven Ones," and Valiērii, its people.
VēdrokesVAY-droh-kessAngrilyBuilt on Vēdros, "Anger," with the -kes suffix, its final -s dropped before the suffix as the established pattern requires.
Vettikesvet-TEE-kessLawfullyBuilt on Vetti, an adjectival form sharing its root with Vettsīrdārdrīvo, "Laws and King's Justice," with the -kes suffix.
VēzikesVAY-zih-kessDailyBuilt on Vēziñ, "Day," with the tongue's -kes suffix; the root's final non-vowel -ñ is dropped before the suffix is added to the remaining vowel.
VȳsīrVEE-SEERGroundedVȳs, "ground," with the perfective suffix -sīr; the suffix's own leading s merges into the root's trailing -s (Vȳs + -sīr → Vȳsīr), the same consonant-merger pattern seen in Rōkes + -sīr → Rōkesīr — no connecting vowel stands between root and suffix; a resultative sense, "grounded."
VȳsōseVEE-soh-sehVysoanBoth noun and adjective: a Vysoan, meaning any person who considers themself of Vysos — by culture, nationality, or species alike — and, of a thing rather than a person, simply "of Vysos." Plural Vȳsōsii.
VȳsōsērVEE-sohs-AY-rThe VysoanVȳsōse with the definite article suffixed, -ēr — the tongue's first attested case of a noun already ending in a bare -e losing that ending before the suffix, rather than carrying both.
ZālarZAH-lahrBurnFirst attested paired with Vēdrogar in the royal liturgy's Vēdrogar Zālar, "Burning Rage."
Zaldrīkeszahl-DREE-kessDraconicBuilt on Zaldrīz, "Dragon," with the -kes suffix.

Verbs

High VysoanPronunciationCommon VysoanMeaning
Amīlah-MEELLead, GuideThe present-tense citation form of Amīl-, standing beside its present-participle Amīlen, "Leading," and its past tense Amīlsīr.
Amīlenah-MEEL-ehnLeading, GuidingThe present-participle form of Amīl-, marked with the tongue's suffix -en.
Amīlōsah-MEEL-OHSLead usAn imperative addressed to the King within the Threefold Devotion, following his style Trēsyvēzos.
Amīlsīrah-MEEL-SEERLedThe past-tense form of Amīl-, marked with the tongue's perfective suffix -sīr.
DrējemāzDRAY-yeh-MAHZShallDrēje-, the prefix form of Drējes, "right, true, correct," with its final -s dropped before the future suffix -māz, as a root's final non-vowel drops before -kes; a future bound by what is right, distinct from the bare future Gamāz, "Will."
DrējesDRAY-yessRight, True, CorrectThe complete form of the root, retaining its final -s when standing alone or used as a suffix, as in Gadrējes; before a vowel suffix or as the first element of a compound it takes the prefix form Drēje-, dropping that -s, as in Drējenēli and Drējemāz — the same pattern governing Vēdros, "Anger," whose prefix form Vēdro- likewise loses its -s in Vēdrogar, "Rage."
GaGAHAct, To Do, To ActThe tongue's bare verb of action, standing alone or as the first element of a productive compound naming a kind of action, as in Gakelin, Gaēdrur, and Gadrējes.
Gamāzga-MAHZWillA general future auxiliary, built with the future suffix -māz atop the root Ga-, standing apart from Samāz, the copula's own future form, "will be."
GiēñimGYAY-nyihmHealRoot of Giēñimenēli, "Healing Ones."
GūrȳdrGOO-REE-durAnnounce FateA compound of Gūrot, "fate, deserved fate," and Ȳdra, "to speak, announce," the two roots shortened by ear where they join; root of Gūrȳdrenēli, "Fate Bringing Ones."
Jemīlyeh-MEELProtectThe present-tense citation form of Jemīl-, standing beside its present-participle Jemīlen, "Protecting," and its past tense Jemīlsīr.
Jemīlenyeh-MEEL-ehnProtectingThe present-participle form of Jemīl-, marked with the suffix -en.
Jemīlōsyeh-MEEL-OHSProtect usAn imperative addressed to the King within the Threefold Devotion, following his style Zaldrīzēr Dorāzmēre.
Jemīlsīryeh-MEEL-SEERProtectedThe past-tense form of Jemīl-, marked with the perfective suffix -sīr.
KosKOHSCanThe tongue's verb of ability.
KosdaorKOHS-dowrCannotKos, "Can," with Daor, "Not," suffixed; the negated form of ability.
Mazīlmah-ZEELLie Down, RestTo lie down, sleep, or rest; of the sun, to set, as in the house's motto Ōsar Vēzos Mazīl Daor, "Our Sun Sets Not."
PryjatPRIH-yahtBreakThe verb "to break"; root of Pryjatsīr, "Shattered," and of Pryjatājoni, "Shattered Islands."
Pryjatsīrprih-yaht-SEERBroken, ShatteredThe past-tense form of Pryjat, marked with the perfective suffix -sīr.
RāeRAH-ehHoldThe verb "to hold"; root of Rāehaer, "Constant," of Rāelagon, "Keeper," and of the royal names Rāeōñ, Rāethel, and Rāethor.
RāehaerRAH-eh-hairConstant, Hold FirmRāe, "Hold," joined to Āer, "Firm," with an h set between the two vowels; both the verb "to hold firm" and the adjective "constant." Root of the royal name Rāehaerys.
RōsīrROH-SEERNamedThe past-tense form of Rō-, marked with the perfective suffix -sīr; the present-tense stem Rōz- loses its final -z before the suffix, exactly as Ūbrem- reduces to Ūbre- in Ūbresīr.
RōzROHZNameBoth verb and noun: the present-tense citation form of the verb "to name" (its stem Rōz- distinct from the shorter Rō- used in the past tense Rōsīr), and the noun "Name" itself — a dual noun/verb precisely as Vȳsōse serves as both noun and adjective. As a noun it takes the genitive suffix -e regularly: Rōz → Rōze, "of Name."
SaSAHAm / To BeThe tongue's copula, serving as both infinitive and present tense; the root from which Sasīr (past) and Samāz (future) are built.
Samāzsa-MAHZWill beThe future-tense form of the copula Sa, marked with the tongue's future suffix -māz.
Sasīrsa-SEERWasThe past-tense form of the copula Sa, marked with the perfective suffix -sīr.
ŪbremOO-bremTeachThe present-tense citation form of the verb "to teach," its stem Ūbrem- distinct from the shorter Ūbre- used in the past tense Ūbresīr.
ŪbremenOO-bre-mehnTeachingThe present-participle form of Ūbrem-, marked with the tongue's ordinary suffix -en, as in Amīlen and Jemīlen.
ŪbremōsOO-bre-MOHSTeach usAn imperative addressed to the King within the Threefold Devotion, following his style Gīmēperzys Nūmāzmēre; built on the present-tense stem Ūbrem-, marked with the suffix -ōs.
ŪbresīrOO-bre-SEERTaughtThe past-tense form of Ūbre-, marked with the perfective suffix -sīr.
ȲdraEE-drahSpeak, AnnounceJoined with Gūrot to form Gūrȳdr-, "to announce deserved fate."
ZālarsīrZAH-lahr-SEERBurnedThe past-tense form of Zālar-, marked with the perfective suffix -sīr.
Zūger Ōñēr VēzoseZOO-gehr oh-NYAY-r vay-ZOH-sehFear the Light of VēzosA central refrain of the royal liturgy. Vēzose is the genitive of Vēzos, the system's own star, "of the Sun" — a near-twin of, but distinct from, Vȳsōse, "Vysoan," which is instead built on Vȳsōs the planet.
ZūgerenZOO-gehr-ehnFearingThe present-participle form of Zūger, marked with the suffix -en.
ZūgersīrZOO-gehr-SEERFearedThe past-tense form of Zūger, marked with the perfective suffix -sīr.

Pronouns & Grammar

High VysoanPronunciationCommon VysoanMeaning
AnaAH-nahOver"Over," in the sense of "set above"; standing also as the prefix ana- in Anaqēlosi, Anavȳsōs, and Anarōvegliss, and within the royal name Āelyxanthor, "Iron Peace over Power."
DaorDOWRNotThe tongue's general negating particle, built on Dao, "No," with an added -r; productive in compounds, as in Kosdaor, "Cannot," and Kelindaor, "No Chance, or Impossible."
ĒurAY-oorYouSecond-person subject and object pronoun, serving both roles without a separate form.
ĒurarAY-oo-rarYourSecond-person possessive adjective, paired directly with the noun it modifies.
ĒureAY-oo-rehYoursSecond-person possessive pronoun, standing alone rather than modifying a noun.
ĒuriAY-oo-rihYou (Plural)Second-person plural subject pronoun, formed by adding the tongue's ordinary plural -i to Ēur.
HenHENAndThe tongue's ordinary coordinating conjunction, joining two words, phrases, or clauses alike.
ĪaEE-ahOr, EitherThe tongue's disjunctive particle, joining two alternatives.
ĪasaEE-ah-sahMaybeBuilt on Īa, "Or, Either," with an added -sa; an adverb of uncertainty standing for an unresolved alternative.
ÑēlNYAYLIFirst-person singular subject pronoun.
ÑesīrNYAY-seerBeforePreposition of time, marking what precedes.
ÑyNYIHMeFirst-person singular object pronoun.
ÑyeNYEHMineFirst-person singular possessive pronoun, standing alone rather than modifying a noun.
ÑykēlaNYIH-KAY-lahMyselfFirst-person singular reflexive pronoun.
ŌsOHSUsFirst-person plural object pronoun.
ŌsarOH-sarOurFirst-person plural possessive adjective, paired directly with the noun it modifies.
ŌsarkēliOH-sar-KAY-lihOurselvesFirst-person plural reflexive pronoun, built on the possessive-adjective stem Ōsar rather than the subject Vī.
ŌseOH-sehOursFirst-person plural possessive pronoun, standing alone rather than modifying a noun.
-rīaREE-ahLand ofA suffix naming a land after its people or quality, as in Valiērīa, "Land of the Proven Ones," and Sȳndorīa.
Skorāskoh-RAHWhereInterrogative pronoun built on the root Skor-, asking a question of place.
Skorēdskoh-RAYDWhenInterrogative pronoun built on the root Skor-, asking a question of time.
Skorēlskoh-RAYLWhoInterrogative pronoun built on the root Skor-, asking after a person.
Skorīskoh-REEWhyInterrogative pronoun built on the root Skor-, asking after a reason.
SkoronSKOH-rohnHowInterrogative pronoun built on the root Skor-, asking after a manner or means.
Skorūtskoh-ROOTWhatInterrogative pronoun built on the root Skor-, asking after a thing.
TāiTAH-eeTheyThird-person plural subject pronoun.
TāiarTAH-ee-arTheirThird-person plural possessive adjective, paired directly with the noun it modifies.
TāieTAH-ee-ehTheirsThird-person plural possessive pronoun, standing alone rather than modifying a noun.
TāikēliTAH-ee-KAY-lihThemselvesThird-person plural reflexive pronoun.
TāixTAH-eeksThemThird-person plural object pronoun.
Tolmāztohl-MAHZAfterPreposition of time, marking what follows.
ŪtOOTItThird-person neuter subject and object pronoun, serving both roles without a separate form.
ŪteOO-tehItsThird-person neuter possessive pronoun, standing alone rather than modifying a noun.
ŪtkēlaOOT-KAY-lahItselfThird-person neuter reflexive pronoun.
VaVAHToThe tongue's preposition for "to," marking direction or purpose.
VīVEEWeFirst-person plural subject pronoun, a suppletive form standing apart from the oblique stem Ōs-, echoing the same subject/oblique split seen in Ñēl/Ñy.
ȲñEENYHerThird-person feminine object pronoun, echoing the feminine suffix -yñ.
ȲñaiEE-nyeeSheThird-person feminine subject pronoun, built by adding -ai to the object stem Ȳñ rather than the reverse.
ȲñeEE-nyehHersThird-person feminine possessive pronoun, standing alone rather than modifying a noun.
ȲñkēlyñEENY-KAY-lihnyHerselfThird-person feminine reflexive pronoun, closing with the feminine noun-class ending -yñ.
ȲsEESHimThird-person masculine object pronoun.
ȲsaiEE-seeHeThird-person masculine subject pronoun, built by adding -ai to the object stem Ȳs rather than the reverse.
ȲseEE-sehHisThird-person masculine possessive pronoun, standing alone rather than modifying a noun.
ȲskēlysEES-KAY-lihsHimselfThird-person masculine reflexive pronoun, closing with the masculine noun-class ending -ys.

Numerals

High VysoanPronunciationCommon VysoanMeaning
AmAHMTenRoot of Amves, "tenth," and of the multiple-of-ten suffix -am, as in Tȳnam, "twenty."
AmiAH-mihTensPlural of Am, "ten," formed like Ēli, "ones," by adding -i.
AmpyrAHM-pihrTen ThousandAm, "ten," joined directly to Pyr, "thousand," without the additive -se- link that forms Amsegār; a straightforward multiplicative compound for the round number ten thousand.
Ampyriahm-PIH-rihTen ThousandsPlural of Ampyr, "ten thousand," formed like Ēli, "ones," by adding -i.
Amsegārahm-seh-GAHRHundred and TenAm, "ten," joined to Gār, "hundred," by the same -se- link as Ēlsegār.
Amsegārvesahm-seh-GAHR-vesHundred and TenthAmsegār, "hundred and ten," with the ordinal suffix -ves.
Amsegārvesērahm-seh-GAHR-ves-AY-rThe Hundred and TenthAmsegārves, "hundred and tenth," with the definite article -ēr.
AmvesAHM-vesTenthAm, "ten," with the ordinal suffix -ves.
AmvesērAHM-ves-AY-rThe TenthAmves, "tenth," with the definite article -ēr.
BȳlBEELSixRoot of Bȳlves, "sixth."
BȳliBEE-lihSixesPlural of Bȳl, "six," formed like Ēli, "ones," by adding -i.
BȳlvesBEEL-vesSixthBȳl, "six," with the ordinal suffix -ves.
BȳlvesērBEEL-ves-AY-rThe SixthBȳlves, "sixth," with the definite article -ēr.
ĒkpyrAYK-pihrMillionPyr, "thousand," raised by the augment Ēk-.
ĒkpyriAYK-pih-rihMillionsPlural of Ēkpyr, "million," formed like Ēli, "ones," by adding -i.
ĒkpyrvesAYK-pihr-vesMillionthĒkpyr, "million," with the ordinal suffix -ves.
ĒkpyrvesērAYK-pihr-ves-AY-rThe MillionthĒkpyrves, "millionth," with the definite article -ēr.
ĒlAYLOneThe tongue's first cardinal numeral; root of Ēlves, "first," Ēlseam, "eleven," Ēlsegār, "hundred and one," and Ēli, "ones." Placed before a noun as a free word, it also serves as the indefinite article, "a/an."
ĒliAY-lihOnesPlural of Ēl, "one." Fused to an ordinal or adjective, it names a kind of being: Ēlves, "first," gives Ēlvesēli, "First Ones"; Giesīr, "hallowed," gives Giesīrēli, "Hallowed Ones."
ĒlseamAYL-seamElevenĒl, "one," with the teen-forming suffix -seam; compare Tȳnseam and Hārseam.
ĒlseamiAYL-seam-ihElevensPlural of Ēlseam, "eleven," formed like Ēli, "ones," by adding -i.
ĒlseamvesAYL-seam-vesEleventhĒlseam, "eleven," with the ordinal suffix -ves.
ĒlseamvesērAYL-seam-ves-AY-rThe EleventhĒlseamves, "eleventh," with the definite article -ēr.
ĒlsegārAYL-seh-GAHRHundred and OneĒl, "one," joined to Gār, "hundred," by a linking -se-; compare Amsegār.
ĒlsegārvesAYL-seh-GAHR-vesHundred and FirstĒlsegār, "hundred and one," with the ordinal suffix -ves.
ĒlsegārvesērAYL-seh-GAHR-ves-AY-rThe Hundred and FirstĒlsegārves, "hundred and first," with the definite article -ēr.
ĒlvesAYL-vesFirstĒl, "one," with the ordinal suffix -ves; compare the ordinals below, each built the same way on its cardinal.
ĒlvesērAYL-ves-AY-rThe FirstĒlves, "first," with the definite article -ēr. Used in the regnal formula, as in Āezāerys, Ēlvesēr Ȳsē Rōz, "Āezāerys, the First of His Name."
GārGAHRHundredRoot of Gārves, "hundredth," and of the compound numerals Ēlsegār and Amsegār.
GāriGAH-rihHundredsPlural of Gār, "hundred," formed like Ēli, "ones," by adding -i.
GārvesGAHR-vesHundredthGār, "hundred," with the ordinal suffix -ves.
GārvesērGAHR-ves-AY-rThe HundredthGārves, "hundredth," with the definite article -ēr.
HārHAHRThreeRoot of Hārves, "third"; Hārseam, "thirteen"; and the magnitude prefix Hār- in Hārēkpyr, "trillion."
HārēkpyrHAHR-AYK-pihrTrillionThe magnitude prefix Hār- (from Hār, "three") joined to Ēkpyr, "million."
HārēkpyriHAHR-AYK-pih-rihTrillionsPlural of Hārēkpyr, "trillion," formed like Ēli, "ones," by adding -i.
HārēkpyrvesHAHR-AYK-pihr-vesTrillionthHārēkpyr, "trillion," with the ordinal suffix -ves.
HārēkpyrvesērHAHR-AYK-pihr-ves-AY-rThe TrillionthHārēkpyrves, "trillionth," with the definite article -ēr.

HārseamHAHR-seamThirteenHār, "three," with the teen-forming suffix -seam.
HārseamiHAHR-seam-ihThirteensPlural of Hārseam, "thirteen," formed like Ēli, "ones," by adding -i.
HārseamvesHAHR-seam-vesThirteenthHārseam, "thirteen," with the ordinal suffix -ves.
HārseamvesērHAHR-seam-ves-AY-rThe ThirteenthHārseamves, "thirteenth," with the definite article -ēr.
HārvesHAHR-vesThirdHār, "three," with the ordinal suffix -ves.
HārvesērHAHR-ves-AY-rThe ThirdHārves, "third," with the definite article -ēr.

Izēkpyriihz-AYK-pih-rihQuadrillionsPlural of Izēkpyr, "quadrillion," formed like Ēli, "ones," by adding -i.
Izēkpyrvesihz-AYK-pihr-vesQuadrillionthIzēkpyr, "quadrillion," with the ordinal suffix -ves.
Izēkpyrvesērihz-AYK-pihr-ves-AY-rThe QuadrillionthIzēkpyrves, "quadrillionth," with the definite article -ēr.
IzulIH-zulFourRoot of Izulves, "fourth," and the magnitude prefix Iz- in Izēkpyr, "quadrillion."
Izuliih-ZUL-ihFoursPlural of Izul, "four," formed like Ēli, "ones," by adding -i.
Izulvesih-ZUL-vesFourthIzul, "four," with the ordinal suffix -ves.
Izulvesērih-ZUL-ves-AY-rThe FourthIzulves, "fourth," with the definite article -ēr.
JētYAYTEightRoot of Jētves, "eighth"; the initial J sounds as the tongue's established Y.
JētiYAY-tihEightsPlural of Jēt, "eight," formed like Ēli, "ones," by adding -i.
JētvesYAYT-vesEighthJēt, "eight," with the ordinal suffix -ves.
JētvesērYAYT-ves-AY-rThe EighthJētves, "eighth," with the definite article -ēr.
PyrPIHRThousandRoot of Pyrves, "thousandth," and of the magnitude series Ēkpyr, Tȳēkpyr, Hārēkpyr, and Izēkpyr.
PyriPIH-rihThousandsPlural of Pyr, "thousand," formed like Ēli, "ones," by adding -i.
PyrvesPIHR-vesThousandthPyr, "thousand," with the ordinal suffix -ves.
PyrvesērPIHR-ves-AY-rThe ThousandthPyrves, "thousandth," with the definite article -ēr.
SīvSEEVSevenRoot of Sīvves, "seventh."
SīviSEE-vihSevensPlural of Sīv, "seven," formed like Ēli, "ones," by adding -i.
SīvvesSEEV-vesSeventhSīv, "seven," with the ordinal suffix -ves.
SīvvesērSEEV-ves-AY-rThe SeventhSīvves, "seventh," with the definite article -ēr.
TōmTOHMFiveRoot of Tōmves, "fifth."
TōmiTOH-mihFivesPlural of Tōm, "five," formed like Ēli, "ones," by adding -i.
TōmvesTOHM-vesFifthTōm, "five," with the ordinal suffix -ves.
TōmvesērTOHM-ves-AY-rThe FifthTōmves, "fifth," with the definite article -ēr.

TȳēkpyriTEE-AYK-pih-rihBillionsPlural of Tȳēkpyr, "billion," formed like Ēli, "ones," by adding -i.
TȳēkpyrvesTEE-AYK-pihr-vesBillionthTȳēkpyr, "billion," with the ordinal suffix -ves.
TȳēkpyrvesērTEE-AYK-pihr-ves-AY-rThe BillionthTȳēkpyrves, "billionth," with the definite article -ēr.
TȳnTEENTwoRoot of Tȳnves, "second"; Tȳnseam, "twelve"; Tȳnam, "twenty"; and the magnitude prefix Tȳ- in Tȳēkpyr, "billion."
TȳnamTEEN-ahmTwentyTȳn, "two," with the multiple-of-ten suffix -am; the tongue's first attested tens numeral.
TȳnamiTEEN-ah-mihTwentiesPlural of Tȳnam, "twenty," formed like Ēli, "ones," by adding -i.
TȳnamvesTEEN-ahm-vesTwentiethTȳnam, "twenty," with the ordinal suffix -ves.
TȳnamvesērTEEN-ahm-ves-AY-rThe TwentiethTȳnamves, "twentieth," with the definite article -ēr.
TȳniTEE-nihTwosPlural of Tȳn, "two," formed like Ēli, "ones," by adding -i.
TȳnseamTEEN-seamTwelveTȳn, "two," with the teen-forming suffix -seam.
TȳnseamiTEEN-seam-ihTwelvesPlural of Tȳnseam, "twelve," formed like Ēli, "ones," by adding -i.
TȳnseamvesTEEN-seam-vesTwelfthTȳnseam, "twelve," with the ordinal suffix -ves.
TȳnseamvesērTEEN-seam-ves-AY-rThe TwelfthTȳnseamves, "twelfth," with the definite article -ēr.
TȳnvesTEEN-vesSecondTȳn, "two," with the ordinal suffix -ves.
TȳnvesērTEEN-ves-AY-rThe SecondTȳnves, "second," with the definite article -ēr.
VōrVOHRNineRoot of Vōrves, "ninth."
VōriVOH-rihNinesPlural of Vōr, "nine," formed like Ēli, "ones," by adding -i.
VōrvesVOHR-vesNinthVōr, "nine," with the ordinal suffix -ves.
VōrvesērVOHR-ves-AY-rThe NinthVōrves, "ninth," with the definite article -ēr.

Interjections

High VysoanPronunciationCommon VysoanMeaning
AiEYEO / HailA vocative interjection addressing the King and the Vysoan people together; first attested in the royal liturgy, carrying no meaning beyond ceremonial address. Also serves a grammatical function: placed before a vocative address that trails its verb rather than leading the sentence, marking it as address rather than a trailing subject (see Word Order & The Vocative Particle).
DaoDOWNoThe tongue's simple negative interjection, standing alone in answer to a question.
KesKESSYesThe tongue's simple affirmative interjection, standing alone in answer to a question.
Vāld SētereVAHLD SAY-teh-rehTree of CreationVāld, "tree," with Sētere, the genitive of Sēter, "form, shape," whose old root Sēte-, "to make," it shares with Sētegqēlosiēr and Sēterenēli; literally "Tree of Form," rendered "Tree of Creation." The tree of the great window's lower register, held by the Covenant as the emblem of all that the Starshaper has made. Definite form Vāldēr Sētere.
Vāldēr SētereVAHLD-AY-r SAY-teh-rehThe Tree of CreationVāld Sētere with the definite article suffixed, -ēr, onto Vāld, the head noun, rather than onto Sētere, its genitive modifier, after the pattern of Dēmysēr Vȳsōse.
Ȳse Qēlosie AnarōveglissEE-seh KAY-loh-sih ah-nah-ROH-veh-glihsHis Sidereal SublimityThe formal style of Sētegqēlosiēr, the Starshaper; built from Ȳse, "His," Qēlosie, "of the Stars" (the genitive plural of Qēlosi, "Stars," formed with the -e suffix as Dohaeririe is from Dohaeriri, and pronounced as the plain plural), and Anarōvegliss, "Sublimity," on the same pattern as the Kardārys's own Ȳse Kardārōñe Rōvegliss. In direct address, Ēurar Qēlosie Anarōvegliss, "Your Sidereal Sublimity."
Ȳse Rōvegliss Ampyr RȳarliEE-seh ROH-veh-glihs AHM-pihr REE-ar-lihHis Majesty, Ten Thousand YearsA celebratory cry wishing the Kardārys a long and successful reign; built from Ȳse, "His," Rōvegliss, "Majesty," Ampyr, "Ten Thousand," and Rȳarli, the plural of Rȳarl, "Year," formed by the tongue's own added-i rule for a noun ending in bare -r.
